organism_context: E. coli / Salmonella CysG is a single chain carrying all three activities; yeast Met8p is bifunctional (dehydrogenase + chelatase, no methyltransferase); Bacillus megaterium SirC and alpha-proteobacterial Sirohydrochlorin ferrochelatase are separate monofunctional proteins.
rationale: The precorrin-2 -> sirohydrochlorin dehydrogenation is run by the C-terminal module of siroheme synthase CysG, which in enterobacteria also carries SUMT methyltransferase and sirohydrochlorin ferrochelatase activity; the dehydrogenase and chelatase even share one active site. Lineages that split the pathway use the monofunctional SirC dehydrogenase.
direction_note: Biosynthetic flux is strictly precorrin-2 -> sirohydrochlorin (the LLM direction); note the ModelSEED entry writes NADP(H) where the enzyme is NAD+-dependent, which biases any thermodynamic direction call toward the reductive side.

organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus SF1293 (bialaphos producer); homologues in phosphinothricin-tripeptide and phosalacine producers.
rationale: Hidaka et al. purified this single 32.8 kDa / 295-residue protein from the bialaphos pathway and showed it performs only the CPEP -> phosphinopyruvate + CO2 rearrangement that forms the C-P bond; no second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: The C-P-bond-forming rearrangement is coupled to decarboxylation and is physiologically irreversible toward phosphinopyruvate; ModelSEED balances this entry with a fictitious 0.5 H2 where the duplicate entry rxn14022 correctly uses H+, inventing a reductant that corrupts the thermodynamic direction call.

organism_context: Salmonella enterica / E. coli CobT is a homodimer with a single PRTase activity; the functionally equivalent archaeal and cyanobacterial system ArsAB is a two-protein complex, not a fused bifunctional enzyme.
rationale: CobT carries one catalytic activity, transfer of the phosphoribosyl group of NaMN onto 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole to give alpha-ribazole-5'-P plus nicotinate. The alternative ArsAB enzyme of methanogens/cyanobacteria is a separate-subunit complex, which does not count as bifunctional.
direction_note: In cobamide biosynthesis CobT runs toward alpha-ribazole-5'-phosphate (the LLM direction); ModelSEED's own status flags this entry short by C11H14N (status MI:C:11/H:14/N:1), so its thermodynamics are not trustworthy.

enzyme_name: Proline utilization A (PutA), proline dehydrogenase module
organism_context: Gram-negative bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella, Bradyrhizobium); in Mycobacterium tuberculosis and in eukaryotes PRODH and P5CDH are separate monofunctional proteins.
rationale: PutA fuses two genuine catalytic activities, FAD-dependent PRODH and NAD+-dependent P5CDH, on one polypeptide with a substrate channel between them; the additional DNA-binding transcriptional-repressor domain of trifunctional PutAs is moonlighting (nucleic-acid binding), not a third catalytic activity, so this stays bifunctional.
direction_note: PRODH is physiologically a one-way catabolic oxidation of proline because its enzyme-bound FADH2 is reoxidised by membrane ubiquinone, and the ModelSEED equation replaces that acceptor with free FAD/FADH2, removing the irreversibility and inverting the predicted direction.

organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus SF1293 and other bialaphos/phosphinothricin producers.
rationale: Same single-activity enzyme as rxn13819 (duplicate ModelSEED entry: cpd17932 and cpd03803 share formula C4H2O7P and KEGG C17946/C06367); the purified protein catalyses only the decarboxylative phosphonomutase rearrangement to (hydroxyphosphinyl)pyruvate.
direction_note: Loss of CO2 makes the rearrangement effectively irreversible in the direction the LLM council chose.

organism_context: Brassicaceae; sinalbin (p-hydroxybenzylglucosinolate) is the Sinapis alba product, and the three characterised Arabidopsis desulfoglucosinolate sulfotransferases are soluble single-domain cytosolic SULTs.
rationale: The final step of core glucosinolate biosynthesis is run by small cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferases (SOT16/17/18 in Arabidopsis, partially purified earlier from Lepidium sativum) that carry only the sulfuryl-transfer activity.
direction_note: Sulfuryl transfer from PAPS to PAP is strongly exergonic and biosynthetically one-way toward the glucosinolate, so ModelSEED's reverse assignment is wrong.

enzyme_name: dTDP-sugar N,N-dimethyltransferase of the TDP-L-megosamine pathway (DesVI/EryCVI-family SAM-dependent sugar N,N-dimethyltransferase)
organism_context: Micromonospora megalomicea megalomicin cluster; TDP-L-megosamine is made from TDP-4-keto-6-deoxy-D-glucose in five steps by MegBVI, MegDII, MegDIII, MegDIV and MegDV, one of which is this N,N-dimethyltransferase.
rationale: The chemistry is the double N-methylation of dTDP-beta-L-daunosamine to dTDP-L-megosamine, a DesVI/EryCVI-type SAM-dependent sugar aminomethyltransferase; two sequential methyl transfers are one catalytic activity, not two, so monofunctional. The exact Meg gene performing this step is not pinned down in the literature consulted, hence low confidence.
direction_note: The SAM -> SAH pair that makes methylation irreversible has been dropped entirely (ModelSEED status MI:C:2/H:4, the two missing methyls), so the stated equation cannot support any direction call; biosynthetically it runs daunosamine -> megosamine as the LLM says.

enzyme_name: No enzyme: KEGG labels R08763 a spontaneous sub-step; the enzymatic overall reaction is o-aminophenol oxidase / phenoxazinone synthase (PhsA)
organism_context: Streptomyces antibioticus phenoxazinone synthase (a multicopper oxidase, actinomycin biosynthesis); actinomycin production persists in phsA-null strains, consistent with the condensation proceeding non-enzymatically.
rationale: KEGG itself annotates R08763 as 'spontaneous', 'incomplete reaction (unidentified acceptor)' and 'the latter part of multi-step reaction' following R08762, so no protein catalyses this particular dimerisation; the dimerisation of two benzoquinone monoimines to the phenoxazinone is the non-enzymatic half of the phenoxazinone synthase mechanism.
direction_note: Oxidative condensation to the aromatic phenoxazinone is effectively irreversible in the forward (LLM) sense, but because the acceptor is undefined and the step is spontaneous the entry should probably not carry a curated direction at all.

enzyme_name: unknown - no enzyme is assigned to this transformation
rationale: KEGG R00744 carries the comment 'unclear reaction, oxidoreduction' with no EC number and no orthology, and no characterised enzyme reduces the free carboxylate of malonyl-CoA to an aldehyde while retaining the thioester; the nearest real chemistry is malonyl-CoA reductase (EC 1.2.1.75), which instead releases CoA and is bifunctional in Chloroflexus aurantiacus but monofunctional in Crenarchaeota.
direction_note: No enzyme is known to run this reaction in either sense, so the gold-grade eQuilibrator direction here is being applied to a transformation the source database itself disowns.

organism_context: Bacillus cereus / B. subtilis MalL and yeast isomaltase are single-domain GH13 hydrolases; the mammalian orthologue sucrase-isomaltase (KEGG K01203) is a single pro-protein carrying both sucrase (EC 3.2.1.48) and isomaltase activities and would count as bifunctional in that lineage.
rationale: In the microbial context ModelSEED models, this isomaltose hydrolysis is run by the monofunctional GH13 oligo-1,6-glucosidase whose structure shows one catalytic (beta/alpha)8 domain; only the intestinal sucrase-isomaltase form carries a second distinct activity.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis is physiologically one-way; ModelSEED drops one of the two glucose products (status MI:C:-6/H:-12/O:-6 versus KEGG's 'isomaltose + H2O <=> alpha-D-glucose + D-glucose'), which is what makes its thermodynamics favour the impossible condensation direction.

organism_context: Streptomyces peucetius daunosamine pathway and the equivalent step of the megalomicin TDP-L-megosamine pathway.
rationale: C-3 transamination of the dTDP-2,6-dideoxy-3-keto-hexose to dTDP-beta-L-daunosamine is performed by a PLP-dependent sugar aminotransferase of the DnrJ/DegT family, a single-activity fold-type I enzyme; enzyme identity is inferred from the pathway chemistry rather than from a direct assay of this exact substrate, hence medium confidence.
direction_note: The amino donor (L-glutamate) and its 2-oxoglutarate product are absent from the equation (ModelSEED status MI:H:4/N:1/O:-1), so the written reaction is not the transaminase reaction and its direction is meaningless; biosynthesis runs toward the aminosugar.

organism_context: Historically described from Aspergillus flavus; the activity in modern organisms is supplied by GH78/GH106 alpha-L-rhamnosidases of fungi (A. oryzae) and gut bacteria that deglycosylate quercitrin to quercetin.
rationale: Quercitrin 3-O-rhamnoside hydrolysis is a single glycoside-hydrolase activity; the characterised alpha-L-rhamnosidases that perform it are one-domain-one-active-site enzymes with no second catalytic function. Enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry plus rhamnosidase literature rather than from a paper on this exact ModelSEED entry.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis is irreversible in vivo; the reverse (rhamnose + quercetin condensation) requires an activated NDP-rhamnose donor and a different enzyme, so ModelSEED's direction is not achievable. ModelSEED also writes beta-L-rhamnose where a retaining rhamnosidase releases the alpha anomer (the rxn15336 variant).

organism_context: Anomer variant of rxn15335; same enzyme, fungal and gut-bacterial GH78/GH106 alpha-L-rhamnosidases.
rationale: Identical chemistry to rxn15335 except that the released rhamnose is the alpha anomer, which is the product a retaining alpha-L-rhamnosidase actually makes; a single hydrolase activity with no second catalytic function.
direction_note: Hydrolysis runs one way; re-forming the rhamnoside would need an activated sugar donor and a glycosyltransferase, not this enzyme.

organism_context: Lodgepole pine (Pinus contorta) xylem enzyme purified and cloned by Dharmawardhana et al.; Arabidopsis BGLU45/46 are the orthologues.
rationale: A family GH1 beta-glucosidase of lignifying xylem with a single catalytic activity; its broad aglycone tolerance (coniferin, syringin, p-coumaryl alcohol glucoside) is one hydrolase activity on several substrates, not two catalytic functions.
direction_note: Hydrolysis of the monolignol glucoside to free coniferyl alcohol is the physiological, irreversible direction; the reverse glucosylation is done by UDP-glucose-dependent UGTs, not by this enzyme.

organism_context: Anomer variant of rxn15348 (alpha-D-glucose written as product); same pine/Arabidopsis GH1 enzyme.
rationale: Same single-activity GH1 beta-glucosidase as rxn15348; note that a retaining GH1 enzyme releases beta-D-glucose, so the alpha-anomer product written here is a post-mutarotation bookkeeping variant rather than the enzymatic product.
direction_note: Hydrolysis is the only direction this enzyme runs.

enzyme_name: unknown - no single enzyme; lumped L-serine to L-cysteine conversion
rationale: KEGG annotates R02818 as a 'multi-step reaction (see R01290, R03260 and R00891)' with no EC and no orthology: it collapses the transsulfuration route (cystathionine beta-synthase then cystathionine gamma-lyase, or the O-acetylserine sulfhydrylase route) into one entry, so no protein catalyses it.
direction_note: The lumped route runs serine -> cysteine (biosynthesis), so ModelSEED's reverse assignment has no pathway behind it; but with the sulfur donor missing (status MI:H:-1/O:-1/S:1) and several enzymes collapsed, this entry should carry no curated direction.

organism_context: Mitochondrial FAD-dependent metabolite-repair enzyme in humans and Drosophila; bacterial and plant counterparts feed electrons to the respiratory chain.
rationale: A single FAD-dependent dehydrogenase activity that oxidises the (R)-2-hydroxyglutarate produced by promiscuous side reactions back to 2-oxoglutarate; it is a classic one-activity metabolite-repair enzyme with no second catalytic function.
direction_note: The enzyme's FAD is tightly bound and reoxidised by an external acceptor (EC 1.1.99.2 is explicitly written with '(acceptor)'), so writing free FAD/FADH2 removes the coupling that makes 2-HG oxidation irreversible and flips the computed direction.

organism_context: Mitochondrial FAD-dependent enzyme; loss-of-function causes L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria. Distinct gene and protein from D2HGDH despite sharing EC 1.1.99.2 in this ModelSEED entry.
rationale: Structural and biochemical characterisation shows a single FAD-dependent oxidation of (S)-2-hydroxyglutarate to 2-oxoglutarate with electron transfer onward to the respiratory chain; one catalytic activity only.
direction_note: As for rxn15407, replacing the physiological electron acceptor with free FAD/FADH2 strips the irreversibility of this metabolite-repair oxidation.

organism_context: Same GH1 monolignol beta-glucosidase as rxn15348; syringin is one of its accepted substrates in lignifying tissue.
rationale: Single GH1 hydrolase activity acting on a second monolignol glucoside; accepting several aglycones is substrate breadth, not a second catalytic function.
direction_note: Hydrolysis to sinapyl alcohol is the physiological, one-way direction; glucosylation is the job of UDP-glucose-dependent UGTs.

organism_context: Anomer variant of rxn15412; same plant GH1 enzyme.
rationale: Identical single-activity GH1 beta-glucosidase; the alpha-D-glucose written as product is a mutarotation bookkeeping variant of the beta anomer a retaining enzyme releases.

organism_context: Same GH1 monolignol beta-glucosidase family as rxn15348/15412, acting on the third monolignol glucoside.
rationale: One hydrolase activity releasing p-coumaryl alcohol for lignin polymerisation; no second catalytic activity is reported for the pine or Arabidopsis enzymes.
direction_note: Hydrolysis is the physiological direction; the reverse requires UDP-glucose and a glycosyltransferase.

organism_context: Anomer variant of rxn15440; same enzyme.
rationale: Same single-activity GH1 beta-glucosidase, with alpha-D-glucose written as the product instead of the beta anomer the retaining mechanism releases.

organism_context: Bacillus subtilis SacB is the reference levansucrase; inulosucrases of lactobacilli make the beta-2,1 polymer. Both are single-domain GH68 five-bladed beta-propellers.
rationale: One transfructosylase active site does everything: polymerisation, hydrolysis of sucrose and the reported 'intrinsic levanase' activity are all fructosyl transfer from the same covalent intermediate to different acceptors, which is one catalytic activity rather than two.
direction_note: The fructan acceptor and its elongated product have been dropped (ModelSEED status MI:C:-6/H:-10/O:-5), leaving 'sucrose -> glucose', which no thermodynamic method can score sensibly; the real reaction is driven irreversibly by the sucrose glycosidic bond energy in the forward (LLM) sense.

organism_context: Anomer variant of rxn15452; same GH68 fructosyltransferase.
rationale: Same single-active-site GH68 fructosyltransferase as rxn15452, with alpha-D-glucose rather than beta-D-glucose written as the released product.
direction_note: As for rxn15452, the fructan acceptor/product pair is missing, so the entry cannot support a thermodynamic direction call.

organism_context: Human liver and kidney peroxisomes; one single branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase handles both the bile-acid intermediates (DHCA-/THCA-CoA) and 2-methyl-branched fatty acyl-CoAs.
rationale: The C24-C25 desaturation of THCA-CoA is catalysed by the peroxisomal branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase, a single acyl-CoA-oxidase activity; the hydratase and dehydrogenase steps that follow sit on a different protein (the D-bifunctional protein HSD17B4), so this enzyme is not itself multifunctional.
direction_note: The real enzyme is an O2-dependent oxidase that discards the electrons as H2O2, which makes the desaturation irreversible; writing free FAD/FADH2 instead (KEGG's own EC 1.3.99.- 'unknown physiological acceptor') removes that driving force and is what lets the thermodynamics point backwards.
